claims.text: Equimolar or near-equimolar CoCrFeNiTi has favorable plasticity and machinability but relatively low hardness and strength.
Ti addition alters the stacking-fault energy of CoCrFeNiTi.
Ti addition modifies local magnetic interactions in CoCrFeNiTi.
Magnetic interactions can affect fcc-hcp phase stability in compositionally related concentrated alloys.
Ti suppresses a stress-induced fcc-to-hcp or other transformation in CoCrFeNiTi.
A dislocation-triggered fcc-to-hcp transformation can provide additional strengthening in related concentrated alloys.
Deformation of single-phase CoCrFeNiTi is dominated by homogeneous dislocation glide.
Phase transformation makes only a minimal contribution to deformation hardening in CoCrFeNiTi.
Nanoscale barrier formation makes only a minimal contribution to deformation hardening in CoCrFeNiTi.
The absence of transformation-induced strengthening and nanoscale obstacles causes the low hardness and strength of CoCrFeNiTi despite its good plasticity.
The applicable starting state is a homogeneous, single-phase, likely fcc CoCrFeNiTi solid solution.
The applicable starting state has a uniform elemental distribution and a defect-free grain structure.
Formation of an hcp phase can mediate transformation-induced strengthening.
CoCrFeNiTi will show little or no initiation of a secondary phase during quasi-static room-temperature deformation.
CoCrFeNiTi will exhibit only modest deformation-induced increases in hardness and strength.
A Ti-free CoCrFeNi comparator will exhibit transformation-induced hardening if the proposed mechanism is active.
The proposed mechanism applies under room-temperature, quasi-static loading to moderate plastic strains.
The proposed mechanism may not apply under high-strain-rate, high-temperature, or multiphase conditions.
A significant stress-induced transformation in CoCrFeNiTi accompanied by hardening comparable to or greater than CoCrFeNi would falsify the proposed Ti-suppression mechanism.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis says suppressing transformation removes extra strengthening and produces low hardness and strength, whereas the predicted outcome ambiguously states that CoCrFeNiTi will have an increase in hardness and strength 'compared to alloys where a transformation provides extra hardening.' If this means a relative increase over transformation-capable alloys, it reverses the proposed causal direction.
